title: Who Got To Stay
type: Paired horizontal bars, two rows (White families, Black families), each bar filling toward a common 0 to 50 percent axis. A faint dotted equity line and a bracketed gap callout between the two bar ends.
data: White families relocated within Hyde Park-Kenwood: 46.1 percent. Black families relocated within Hyde Park-Kenwood: 16.8 percent. Gap: 29.3 points, roughly a 2.7-to-1 ratio. Figures are for the Hyde Park A and B projects. Render the two bars to the SAME percent scale (axis 0 to 50). White bar reaches 46.1, Black bar reaches 16.8. Show each value as a count-up number at the bar tip.
source: University of Chicago, Committee on Environment, Geography and Urbanization (CEGU), 'The Toasters of Hyde Park A,' Expositions Magazine, Nov 28 2023 (cegu.uchicago.edu/2023/11/28/hyde-park-a-toaster-buildings). Verified against the CEGU primary text, which reads 46.1 percent of white families and 16.8 percent of Black families relocated within the neighborhood. Note the source figure is 16.8 percent, not the 16.6 percent transcribed in hp-research.json.
animation: Over ~5s. Both bars start at zero width on cream. The two grids and row labels (Gill Sans small caps) fade in first over 0.6s. White bar wipes rightward to 46.1 percent in forest green over 1.6s with an ease-out, its tip number counting 0 to 46.1. A 0.4s hold, then the Black bar wipes to 16.8 percent in rust over 1.4s, number counting 0 to 16.8, deliberately stopping far short of the first bar so the shortfall reads physically. Then a thin bracket draws between the two bar tips over 0.8s and the gap label '29.3 points' fades up. Built in PIL by drawing rounded rectangles per frame at increasing width; the count-up is per-frame drawtext. No bounce, no easing flourish.
layout: 1920x1080, deep cream #f5f0e8 ground with a faint forest baseline grid. Top-left eyebrow in Gill Sans, letterspaced small caps rust: 'HYDE PARK A & B, 1955 TO 1970'. Title 'Who Got To Stay' in Baskerville ~96px forest, upper third, left aligned to a 240px left margin. Two bar rows centered vertically, each ~110px tall, separated by ~80px. Row labels left of each bar in Baskerville ~44px ink: 'White families' over the forest bar, 'Black families' over the rust bar. Bars share a left origin at x=620 and a 50-percent scale ending near x=1560; axis ticks at 0/25/50 in faint warm gray below. Value numbers sit just past each bar tip in Baskerville ~64px matching the bar color. A vertical bracket and the gap note '29.3 points, about 2.7 to 1' sit at far right in ink ~36px. Bottom-left source credit in Gill Sans ~24px warm gray: 'Source: University of Chicago CEGU, Constructing a Compatible Community, 2023'. Generous margins, one accent color per bar, no gridline clutter, museum restraint.

title: The Great Migration Reaches Chicago
type: Area-over-time (filled curve) with four anchored census-year markers, rising left to right, plus a large terminal count-up number.
data: Chicago Black population by U.S. Census year. 1910: 44,103 (about 40,000). 1920: 109,458. 1930: 233,903 (about 234,000). 1940: 277,731 (about 278,000). Plot the four points on a time axis 1910 to 1940 and a population axis 0 to ~300,000; fill the area beneath the curve. Headline framing 'about 40,000 in 1910 to about 278,000 by 1940.'
source: U.S. Decennial Census via Encyclopedia of Chicago, 'African Americans,' and History of African Americans in Chicago, Wikipedia. Exact counts 44,103 / 109,458 / 233,903 / 277,731 confirmed across multiple sources (BlackDemographics, NPS Black Metropolis). Round figures 40,000 and 278,000 match the census and hp-research.json.
animation: Over ~6s. Time axis (1910 to 1940) and four faint vertical year guides draw first over 0.8s in warm gray. The filled area then sweeps left to right as a clip-mask reveal over 3s, the forest fill rising and steepening visibly between 1920 and 1930 to convey acceleration. As the leading edge passes each census year, a small rust dot lands and that year's value fades up beside it (44,103 then 109,458 then 233,903 then 277,731), so the numbers arrive in sequence like footfalls. In the final 1.4s a large terminal number in the upper right counts up 40,000 to 278,000 in Baskerville and the curve's end point pulses once. Built in PIL with a per-frame horizontal reveal mask over a precomputed polyline-and-fill; count-ups are per-frame drawtext. Optional very slow 2.5D parallax drift on the whole plate to match the film's archival treatment.
layout: 1920x1080, cream ground. Eyebrow Gill Sans small caps rust top-left: 'CHICAGO, U.S. CENSUS 1910 TO 1940'. Title 'The Great Migration Reaches Chicago' in Baskerville ~88px forest across the top, left aligned at 200px margin. Plot occupies the lower two-thirds: x-axis years 1910/1920/1930/1940 labeled in Gill Sans ~34px ink along the bottom; y-axis implied, no boxed frame. Filled area in forest green #122119 at ~85 percent opacity with a 1.5px darker top stroke; rust #c55d3e marker dots at each census node. Each node value in Baskerville ~40px ink sits above its dot. The terminal headline number '278,000' in Baskerville ~150px forest anchors the upper-right negative space, with a Gill Sans kicker beneath it ~30px warm gray reading 'up from about 40,000 in 1910.' Source credit bottom-left Gill Sans ~24px warm gray: 'Source: U.S. Census via Encyclopedia of Chicago'. One curve, two colors, lots of air.

title: The Plan On Paper
type: Three sequential count-up stat blocks (acres, buildings, families) with a small unit-dot motif under the families figure, presented as a triptych rather than a multi-series chart.
data: Hyde Park-Kenwood Urban Renewal Plan as approved Nov 7 1958: 856 acres included; 638 buildings to be demolished; about 4,000 families displaced. The South West Hyde Park clearance land was nearly 80 percent Black at acquisition.
source: Hyde Park Herald, 'Lost Hyde Park: Land clearance'; University of Chicago Library, 'Renewal and Revival' Centennial exhibit; New York Times obituary of Julian Levi (1996); CEGU, Constructing a Compatible Community (2023). The 856 acres / 638 buildings / ~4,000 families and the nearly 80 percent Black figure are all confirmed; hp-research.json rates each high confidence.
animation: Over ~5.5s, staggered. Three stat blocks animate in sequence left to right, each ~1.2s apart. For each, the big number counts up from zero in Baskerville (0 to 856, 0 to 638, 0 to about 4,000) while its label fades up beneath. After the third number lands, a quiet row of small rust unit-dots fades in under the families figure with a single short line of type, 'cleared land in South West Hyde Park was nearly 80 percent Black,' to give the abstract counts a human anchor. Built in PIL as per-frame drawtext count-ups plus a static dot row; no spin or bounce. The 80-percent note appears as plain type, not a second chart, to keep the frame from feeling busy.
layout: 1920x1080, cream ground, used only if a third beat is wanted; otherwise the two charts above carry the data load. Eyebrow Gill Sans small caps rust top-center: 'HYDE PARK-KENWOOD RENEWAL PLAN, APPROVED NOV 7 1958'. Title 'The Plan On Paper' Baskerville ~80px forest, centered upper third. Three evenly spaced columns across the middle band, each with a large number in Baskerville ~140px (col 1 and 2 forest, col 3 rust for the human figure): '856' / '638' / '4,000'. Under each, a Gill Sans ~34px ink label: 'acres included' / 'buildings to be demolished' / 'families displaced'. Thin vertical hairline dividers in faint warm gray between columns. Below the third column, a single line in Gill Sans ~30px ink and a short rust dot row. Source credit bottom-center Gill Sans ~24px warm gray: 'Source: Hyde Park Herald; University of Chicago Library; CEGU'. Symmetric, restrained, architectural.
